This is a beautiful and dazzling scene, depicting a great cosmic event, and it is a prelude to an even greater event.

"The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split" (54:1). Imam al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab, from Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The people of Makkah demanded of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he show them a miracle. So he showed them that the moon split in two, and Hira was between the two halves." This narration has also been reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim through other chains from Qatadah and Anas (رضي الله عنه). The narration of Jubayr ibn Mut'im has been reported by Imam Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sulayman ibn Kathir, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the moon split in two. One piece was seen on a mountain and the other on that mountain." Then the disbelievers said, "Muhammad has cast a spell upon us. If he has cast a spell upon us, he cannot cast a spell upon all the people of the world." This narration is reported in this manner by Imam Ahmad alone. Imam al-Bayhaqi, in his book al-Dala'il, has narrated it through Muhammad ibn Kathir, his brother Sulayman ibn Kathir, and Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman. Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi have also reported it from Jubayr ibn Mut'im (رضي الله عنه) through other routes and chains.

The narration of Abdullah ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه): Imam al-Bukhari narrated it: from Yahya ibn Kathir, from Bakr, from Ja'far, from Urak ibn Malik, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه), who said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the event of the moon splitting into two took place." Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim also narrated it through a previous chain via Urak ibn Malik from Ibn Abbas. Imam Ibn Jarir narrated, through another chain via Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه): "It happened in this way: before the Hijrah the moon split until people saw that it was in two pieces." Awfi also narrated in this manner from Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه). Tabarani narrated through another chain via Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه), who said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah the moon was darkened." Then the people of Makkah said, "Muhammad has cast a spell even upon the moon." Upon this, this verse was revealed:

"And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, 'Continuous magic'" (54:2). The narration of Abdullah ibn Umar: The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi says: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qadi narrated from al-Jarawi, both from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri, from Wahb ibn Jarir, from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, and from Abdullah ibn Umar (رضي الله عنه), in the interpretation of this verse:

"The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split" (54:1). He said: "This happened in the time of the Messenger of Allah. It split in two, one part was behind a mountain and one part was in front." Upon this, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allahumma ishhad" (O Allah, bear witness). In this manner, this narration has been reported by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, and from Mujahid.

The narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه): Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan ibn Abi Nujayh narrated to us from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه), who said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the moon split in two. The disbelievers saw it clearly." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Ishhadu" (Bear witness). Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim narrated this same report from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar Abdullah ibn Sakhbarah, from Ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه). Imam al-Bukhari says that Imam Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it from Abu 'Awanah, from Mughirah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه), who said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the moon split in two. The Quraysh said, 'This is the magic of Ibn Abi Kabshah.'" It is said that the people said, "Look, let those who are traveling come, for Muhammad cannot cast a spell upon all the people of the world." So after that, those who were traveling came, and they also confirmed it. Imam al-Bayhaqi has narrated it by other routes from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and the meaning is similar.

These are the mutawatir (widely transmitted) narrations, through various chains and routes, that this event occurred, and its location in Makkah has also been identified. Except for one narration, which mentions Mina, the other narrations concern Makkah. The event took place in the time of the Prophet ﷺ and before the Hijrah. Most narrations state that it split in two, and one narration states that it was an eclipse of the moon. Whatever the nature of the event, it is established by the narrations, and the narrations also specify the time and place and determine the form of the splitting of the moon.

This was such an event that the Holy Qur'an presented it to the polytheists as evidence for the Resurrection. No narration has been transmitted from the polytheists denying the event itself. Therefore, the event must have occurred in this way, and so many people must have seen it that it was no longer possible for them to deny the event itself, even if out of arrogance and pride. If there had been any way for them to deny it, they would certainly have done so. The reports and comments transmitted from the disbelievers are that Muhammad ﷺ has cast a spell, but even among them the wise people said, "Look into it." After investigating travelers, they came to know that it was not a lie, because if the people of Makkah could be bewitched by Muhammad ﷺ, he could not bewitch the whole world; and when they asked the travelers who had come from outside Makkah, they too confirmed it.

Now the question remains whether the polytheists demanded a sign from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. In response, the miracle of the splitting of the moon occurred. This narration in fact contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an. The implication is that the Prophet ﷺ was not given miracles of the kind given to the earlier prophets, and this had a specific and particular cause.

"And We did not refrain from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them" (17:59). The meaning is that it is Allah's decision that the Prophet was not given the miracles that were demanded.

Whenever the disbelievers demanded miracles from the Prophet ﷺ, the answer given was that presenting miracles is not among his duties, and that Muhammad ﷺ is only a human being and a Messenger, and that everywhere the Holy Qur'an alone was declared to be his miracle, and a challenge was issued to bring a surah or book like it.

"Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like, even if they were to help one another" (17:88). "We have explained in this Qur'an for the people in various ways, but most people refused and persisted in disbelief, and they said, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of dates and grapes and cause rivers to flow through it, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring God and the angels before us face to face, or a house of gold comes to be for you, or you ascend into the sky, and we will not believe even your ascent until you bring down upon us a writing that we can read.'" Say, "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?" (17:90–93). Therefore, to say that the miracle of the splitting of the moon came in response to the disbelievers' demand is contrary to several texts of the Qur'an, and also contrary to the principle that in this world the final message presents to humanity only the Qur'an, and that the inimitability of the Qur'an is its miracle, and that through the Qur'an the human heart and mind are directed toward the signs and miracles that exist within the self, that are abundant in the horizons, and that are abundant in human history and are highly instructive. As for the miracles that occurred at the hands of the Prophet ﷺ and that have been confirmed by authentic narrations, they were given to the Prophet ﷺ as an honor, not given as proofs of prophethood.

This is why the miracle of the splitting of the moon occurred. The Qur'anic text has confirmed it, it has been confirmed in mutawatir narrations, the place and time in which it occurred has been determined, and the details of the manner in which it occurred are also present. But regarding the narrations that state its cause, we remain silent. We simply say that the splitting of the moon indicates the nearness of the Resurrection, and in it is a lesson for us that we should be alert, awake, and prepare for that great hour. Therefore, the splitting of the moon was a cosmic miracle, and the Qur'an directed humans to it, just as the Qur'an directs attention to other cosmic miracles; and just as their attitude toward other miracles is astonishing, so too they derived no benefit from this miracle.

Miracles that break habit belong to the early stages of humanity. They certainly impressed people in an age when humanity had not progressed so far in knowledge that it could understand the miracles established and scattered throughout this universe and be impressed by them. The miracles that occurred at the hands of past prophets and by which humanity was impressed belong to an age when humanity had not reached the level of intellectual maturity; but today, in this universe, humanity has come to know such miracles that are greater than those miracles. Although they do not impress those who still hold those primitive sentiments and have not reached the level of intellectual maturity.

Suppose the splitting of the moon was a miracle; the moon itself is also a miracle. This celestial body, with its size, its present form, shape, nature, the stages of its orbit, its cycles, its effects, its influence on life on earth, and its floating in the atmosphere without any support, is this not a great miracle that is constantly established and enduring, and is before our observation, and about which we can think at all times? From it we take lessons. Is any greater proof of divine power needed? Who can deny the miracle of the moon itself, except one who is obstinate and stubborn?

The Qur'an has placed humanity before this universe and made it observe that great miracles are constantly established and enduring within this universe. The Qur'an wants to connect humanity constantly with these miracles. It does not mean that something like the splitting of the moon is shown once in thousands of years and is seen only by the people of one time. The Qur'an says: look at this universe, if you have eyes that take lessons.

This whole universe is a panorama of miracles. It remains before the eyes and does not disappear, and see all these miracles and keep on seeing. Among them are small miracles and great ones, and these miracles bear witness. Listen to their testimony. It is a wondrous testimony; record it. It is an extremely beautiful testimony, containing both beauty and perfection, and it not only brings a person to a decision but also leaves him awestruck and astonished, and as a result a very firm faith is produced, profound and serious.

At the beginning of this surah there is an indication that the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split, which deeply affects a person, because the establishment of the Resurrection and the splitting of the moon are very great events. The Qur'an shows that you have already witnessed this great event, and in the same way the Resurrection will also take place.

Regarding the Resurrection alone after the splitting of the moon, Imam Ahmad narrated from Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Mutarrif, from Abu Hazim, and from Sahl ibn Sa'd (رضي الله عنه), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he joined his middle finger and index finger to indicate it (agreed upon).

Despite the fact that the Hour has drawn near, and that they have witnessed this most impressive event with their own eyes, and have seen the signs of Allah in various forms, yet hatred was filled to overflowing in the hearts of these people. They insisted upon the path of misguidance. They were not affected by warning, nor were they affected by the signs scattered throughout this universe, which are sufficient for admonition and can keep a person from denying. But these people did not benefit from them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 2:

وان یروا ............ تغن النذر (54:2) "But whatever sign they see, they turn away and say, 'This is continuous magic.' They denied and followed their own desires. Every matter will reach its destination. There have already come to them accounts that contain sufficient deterrent from rebellion, and a wisdom that fully fulfils the purpose of admonition, but warnings do not benefit them."

Regarding the splitting of the moon as well, they turned away and said the same thing they used to say about the verses of the Quran, that it is an extremely effective magic. They call one sign magic, and regarding successive signs they say that this is continuous magic whose series never ends. These people are turning away from contemplating the signs of Allah. They turn away from the indication and testimony of the signs as well. They make this denial only being compelled by their desires, not because they have any proof, nor is there any proof against Islam, given that they have contemplated the universe spread around them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 3:

"Every matter will reach its settled end" (54:3). In this great universe, every thing is placed in its proper position, and it is firm in its place. It does not waver, and there is no unrest within it. Every matter of this universe is based upon stability and permanence. It is not the case that principles change in accordance with shifting desires, and that rules and laws alter like the capricious moods of kings. Nor is it the case that affairs here are settled by chance and accident. Everything occurs in its own place and at its own appointed time. A person should observe that in his environment, in time and space, in events and occurrences, there is an order, and this order and principle is visible in everything. In the revolution of the heavens, in the ways of life, in the growth of animals and plants, in all objects and substances, and even in the functions and duties of their own bodies and in the working of their organs, there is an order, and they have no control over these things. This firmness and stability encompasses them, surrounds all things around them, and is seen before them and behind them on every side. It is only human beings who are restless, and who, according to their desires, sometimes go this way and sometimes that way.

The passage is Sayyid Qutb's commentary on 54:4, and it opens with a Qur'anic quotation that is cut off in the source ("ولقد ............ مزدجر"), so I render the quoted verse as the text gives it.

"And there has certainly come to them news (of the earlier nations) containing sufficient deterrence."

These people have already been met with circumstances that contain ample lessons to keep them from rebellion. The Qur'an has repeatedly and in varied ways related reports about the signs (ayat) of this universe. News has also come to them about the deniers (mukadhdhibin) of earlier great nations. And news of the Hereafter has come to them in the form of scenes of the Resurrection. In all these matters there are lessons, warnings, and signs of danger, and within them are wise words that enter the heart directly, along with good guidance. But hearts that have gone blind do not see the signs, do not benefit from these reports, and neither take lessons from the news nor fear the warning.

Hikmah ........ an-nudhur (54:5) "And wisdom that fully accomplishes the purpose of admonition, yet warnings do not benefit them." Faith is the blessing by which the human heart benefits from these things.

After portraying in such detail their aversion and their persistence in disbelief, and after making clear that they do not benefit even from news, warnings are of no use to them either. The Messenger (ﷺ) is addressed, bidding him to turn away from them as well and leave them to their own state. That Day is approaching quickly; the splitting of the moon was a sign of that Day, and that Day is very near.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verses 6–8:

"So turn away from them, [O Prophet], on the day when the caller calls to a dreadful thing. They will come out of the graves with eyes humbled, as if they were scattered locusts, rushing toward the caller. The disbelievers will say, 'This is a difficult day.'" (54:6–8)

This is one of the scenes of that Day. Its terror and its intensity are suited to the theme, atmosphere and tone of this surah; they are suited as a prelude to the approach of the Hour, and also to the report that the moon was split, and they harmonize with the rhythm found within the surah.

This scene moves very swiftly and is in harmony with the atmosphere. It is clearly visible and full of motion, and its movements and manner are also balanced. People are emerging from the graves in groups, scattering like a swarm of locusts. This image becomes even clearer through the comparison with the locust swarm. This group is cowering in fear. Their eyes are lowered from humiliation and dread. They are rushing toward the caller, wanting to know what calamity has befallen them. They do not know what is about to happen. There is extreme unease; those who go toward a terrible end can only say this much.

"This is a difficult day" (54:8). This is the speech of a person in extreme anguish and exhaustion, one who advances with heavy steps as if walking to the gallows. This is the day that is about to come, yet these people are sunk in heedlessness and turn away from the warning. They deny the truth. O Prophet, you too turn away from them, and leave them to their end, which is extremely frightful.

Having opened the surah with such a terrifying manner and forceful tone, and after presenting a frightful scene of the Resurrection, the surah now presents some scenes from human history. Those upon whom a calamity like the one shown in the above scene befell, these nations too adopted the same attitude as the people of Makkah have adopted. Beginning with the people of Noah (peace be upon him).

Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran), on Surah 54, verse 9:

"The people of Noah denied before them: they denied Our servant and said, 'He is mad,' and he was rebuked."

Before them, the people of Noah denied: they denied the signs of Allah as well as the messengership.

Fa-kadhdhabu 'abdana (54:9): "They denied Our servant." That is, Noah.

Wa-qalu majnun (54:9): "And they said, 'He is mad.'" Just as the Quraysh said of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was mad, they also threatened Noah that they would stone him, and they tormented him by mockery. They demanded of him that he cease criticising them, and they gave him severe threats and harsh reproaches.

Wa-izdujir (54:9): "And he was harshly rebuked." Although it would have been appropriate for them to refrain themselves and obey him.

Having reached this point, Noah turned to his Lord in supplication, because it was Allah Who had sent him on this mission, so that he might give his Lord the report that his people had treated him in this manner, that he had striven this hard, and that now his strength had given way. He called upon Allah at a time when neither any stratagem remained nor any power. He had tried every means.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 54, verse 10:

﴿Then he called upon his Lord: "I am overcome, so help [me]."﴾ (54:10) At last he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so take vengeance upon them." My strength is finished. I have made my full effort. My powers have given way, and this is now Your task. Denial and disbelief have prevailed over me. Therefore, You alone must help. O Allah, now You alone take vengeance upon them. Take revenge for Your call. Support the truth. Help Your own system; You alone must help it. The command is Yours, the struggle is for You, and my role has now ended. When Hadrat Nuh (ʿalayhi as-salam) said this, and the matter was handed over by the Messenger of God to the Lord, who is the Compeller and the Subduer, the hand of divine power began its work, and the earth was cleared of them. The chastisement of God began to move in such a way that all the natural forces started doing their work.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 11:

ففتحنا ............ امر قدقدر (54:12) "Then We opened the gates of heaven with torrential rain, and split the earth into springs, and the waters met for a matter that had already been decreed." (54:11-12)

This is a great cosmic movement, very forceful, yet the picture of this great cosmic process and movement is drawn in a few words. The words have been chosen very beautifully, and it is told about this whole process that all of it is the work of Divine power.

ففتحنا ابواب السماء (54:11) "with torrential rain": that is, rain in which water pours down heavily, with this same force and this same movement.

And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs. (54:12)

The scene of the earth being split open and springs gushing forth is such that from every place fountains burst out. Springs appeared everywhere, and nothing but springs could be seen.

Now the water pouring down violently from the heavens and the water welling up from the earth came together.

﴿So the waters met for a matter that had been decreed﴾ (54:12). That is, the purpose of both was that the predetermined matter be fulfilled. Both waters were working under the direction of Divine power.

This water took the form of a flood. The earth was covered over, and the filth that existed on the earth in the form of human beings was cleansed. The Messenger of God had despaired of this purification; in his view these people had become beyond cure. But the benevolent hand of God's power reached them. The Messenger's supplication was accepted. The whole universe was set in motion, and the Messenger and his companions received deliverance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 13:

"And We carried him upon a [vessel] of planks and nails, running under Our eyes. That was a reward for one who had been rejected." This passage shows that it was a very great ship. It was made of planks and nails. The attributes of the ship are mentioned, and its name is not mentioned. To show its greatness, it is then said that this ship sails under Allah's care. It is under Allah's watchful eye.

Retribution for the one who was disbelieved (the one who was denied his due), in recompense for the one who was rejected. His call was not merely denied; he was also insulted and abused. These people inflicted persecution upon the Prophet. This is their punishment. They mocked the Prophet. Allah bestowed this honour upon him.

From this we learn how the powers of Allah operate in support of the one who is left helpless in the way of Allah, and how Allah takes retribution when a person, having completed his task and expended his full strength, entrusts the matter to Allah. All the powers of this universe rise up in his support, and behind these powers stands Allah Himself, with His power and majesty.

At the conclusion of this scene of dreadful vengeance and this decisive outcome, those who witnessed this sight with their own eyes are addressed: Take heed from these events, so that perhaps, being impressed, they will accept the call to truth.

"We left it as a sign. So is there anyone who will take heed?" This event, with all its circumstances, We preserved in the record of history so that it would be a sign for those who come after.

"So is there anyone who will take heed?" (Fa-hal min muddakir): is there anyone who will accept admonition and act upon it? It is a question meant to awaken hearts: what was the punishment, and what was the end of those who were warned?

So how were My punishment and My warnings? (54:16)

Thus it happened, just as the Quran has depicted it. It was a severely destructive punishment that annihilated all the criminals and made the warning of the one who warned come true. This is the Quran's manner of expression: extremely easy, comprehensible, and highly attractive to the reader, so that everyone may read it and reflect. It possesses the attraction of plain truth, is in accordance with human nature, and is exciting for every disposition, and its wonders never come to an end. Read it again and again, and it will appear new each time. Whenever anyone reflects upon it, they will find a new meaning and a new insight. The more any human soul keeps company with it, the more its love will increase.

﴿We have indeed made the Qur'an easy for remembrance; so is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ (45:17)

This is the lesson repeated at the end of every paragraph. After each vivid scene, and after every historical end that befell those who denied (al-mukadhdhibin), the Qur'an speaks to the human heart, calling it to accept admonition, to acquire understanding, and to reflect.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 18:

﴿Kadhdhabat ʿAad, fa-kayfa kana ʿadhabi wa nudhur﴾ (54:18 to 22): "ʿAad denied, so see how was My punishment and how were My warnings. We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of continuous ill-omen, which was tearing people away as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees. So see how was My punishment and how were My warnings. We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance; so is there anyone who will take heed?"

This is the second paragraph, and it presents the second scene of the punishment that befell the earlier nations. After the people of Nuh, the destruction of ʿAad was the next great calamity. The people of Nuh were destroyed first, and after them ʿAad.

First it is stated that ʿAad also denied, but before the verse ends, a fearful question is posed: ﴿Fa-kayfa kana ʿadhabi wa nudhur﴾ (54:18, 45:81): "How was My punishment and how were My warnings?" After this it is told that their end came in such a manner: dreadful and terrifying.

We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of continuous misfortune, which was snatching people up and casting them down like the trunks of uprooted date palms.

The word ṣarṣar (ریحاصرصرا, Q. 41:16) means a cold, harsh wind. The very rhythm of the words indicates its nature. Naḥs means ill-omened, and consider what kind of misfortune a people would be given, and how great that misfortune was, that was given to ʿĀd. Thus the scene was that just as a harsh wind uproots date palm trunks from their roots and they fall to the ground, and the tree lies flattened in a terrible way, so these people lay scattered across the plains.

The scene is extremely frightening. The wind is harsh, and this wind that was sent upon the ʿĀd was one of the armies of Allah, one force among the forces of this universe: a creation of Allah, a force operating in exact accordance with Allah's law of nature, a force that Allah may impose upon whomever He wills. This force moves through the deserts, and when it reaches the settlements of ʿĀd, it brings them to the state described above.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 23:

The tribe of Thamud emerged in the Arabian Peninsula after 'Ad. Like 'Ad, it was unmatched in strength and grandeur. However, the 'Ad were in the south and the Thamud were in the north. The Thamud also denied the Messenger in the same way that 'Ad had denied him, even though the Thamud knew well the fate of 'Ad, since they lived in the south of the Arabian Peninsula.

﴿They said: "Shall we follow a single human being from among us? If we did so, we would indeed be in error and madness."﴾ (54:24) "Is it that the reminder has been sent down upon him alone from among us? No, rather he is a great liar and an insolent one."

This is the same doubt that has troubled the hearts of all who deny throughout history.

﴿Has the reminder been cast upon him alone from among us?﴾ (54:25) This was their hollow and baseless arrogance, and a person who has such arrogance within him can never see the truth. He does not look at the matter; he looks only at who is saying it.

﴿A single human being from among us, shall we follow him?﴾ (54:24)

What is wrong with Allah choosing one individual from among His servants? Allah knows very well where to place the trust of prophethood, and then He sends down the reminder upon him, gives him guidance, and sends down words of admonition upon him. Allah is the Creator. He knows to whom among His servants He has given the capacity for this trust. Moreover, it is Allah who sends down the reminder. This question is a baseless one and a foolish babble, the kind that can arise only in the minds of extremely misguided people. Such people, regarding any call, do not consider how much truth and sincerity it contains. They look at the one who gives the call and ask how great a man he is among the two towns. If the word of a little man is accepted, he will become great, and these people will remain small.

This is why such people have always said this.

ابشر ........ وسحر (45:4 2) "Shall we follow a single man from among us? Then we would indeed be in error and madness." If we followed this lone man who is one of us, its meaning would be that we have strayed, our intellect has been struck, or we have fallen into Hell. If this disbelieving act had occurred among us, when intellect is destroyed a person regards guidance as misguidance, and thinks that he will enter what is, as it were, Hells of great number. (The word سعر is the plural of سعیر, "sa'ir," meaning a blazing fire.) Yet by accepting the call he would have come under the shade of faith, but he thinks that if he believes he will enter the Hells.

This is why they said of the Messenger whom Allah had sent to guide them that he was a liar and a seeker of gain.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 25:

"Rather, he is a liar, an arrogant one." (54:25)

"Kadhdhab" means a liar, and "ashir" means one who is greatly covetous and grasping. Through this preaching, he seeks authority and status. Every caller (da'i) to Islam is always accused of this same charge: that under the pretext of the Islamic call, he strives to obtain worldly interests. This is the position of those blind people who are unaware of the feelings of righteous people and the inner motives of their hearts.

The narrative has so far proceeded in the manner of a story and an account, when suddenly the address (khitab) comes into the matter, and it appears as though the events are still ongoing. Therefore, it is told what is about to happen soon, and they are threatened with events that will take place in the future.

The commentary cites a verse (Surah al-Qamar 54:26 refers to the same theme; the passage quotes 45:62 here). Translating as it stands:

"Soon they will know who is the utter liar and the greedy one." This is a Qur'anic method of narrating stories. This style breathes life into the narrative: rather than being merely a tale of the past, the imagination's force transforms that story into a scene. Now it is no longer a story, but becomes events of the present and future.

"Soon they will know who is the utter liar and the greedy one." Tomorrow this reality will be unveiled, they will not be able to escape, and this calamity will show who is the liar and what the punishment of liars is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 54, verses 27–28:

"Verily, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them. So watch them, and be patient. And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each drinking turn about." [Note: the Urdu quotation of the verses is rendered here as the commentary quotes it.]

Now the reader waits to see what happens. The she-camel is sent forth. It is a trial for them and a test: who will succeed and who will fail. The Messenger of the time also waits to see what will happen, and in accordance with Allah's command he exercises patience until the outcome of the test becomes apparent. The Prophet is given the guidance that the water is divided between them and the she-camel. This she-camel was certainly a specific she-camel. The division was such that one day the entire water was for the she-camel and the next day for them. The she-camel will come on her day, and these people will come on their days. She will drink on her day, and these people will take water on their days.

Now the context again takes on the style of narrative and story, and after this the events come in this manner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 29:

﴿Then they called their companion, and he took up the task and slew she-camel.﴾ (54:29) And this man was one of the mischief-makers who were the root of corruption in that city. Concerning them, it is mentioned in Surah An-Nahl (27:48–49): ﴿And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform.﴾ And in Surah Ash-Shams (91:12), it is said: ﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth.﴾

Some narrations mention that this man drank wine so that he might carry out this deed with boldness and slay the she-camel which Allah had sent as a sign, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had warned them and made them aware that if they harmed her, the punishment of Allah would overtake them. Thus, according to this, the meaning of "fa-ta'āṭā" (﴿so he took up the task﴾, cf. 54:29) would be "drinking wine" rather than "taking up the task."

﴿Then they called their companion, and he took [the task] and slew her﴾ (54:29). Either he took up this responsibility, or he slew her after drinking wine. This became the test, and the punishment descended upon them.

"So how was My punishment and how were My warnings?" (Qur'an 54:16 and related verses). This question is asked to create a sense of wonder and fear, and it comes before the mention of the punishment itself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 31:

إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا ... الْمُحْتَظِرِ (54:31)... "We sent upon them but a single blast, and they became like the dry crumbled remains of a pen-builder's enclosure" (54:31). [Note: this translation carries the Qur'anic text as quoted in the commentary; the Urdu passage begins with the verse 45:13 citation as given.]

The Urdu passage as it stands reads: "We sent upon them but a single blast, and they became like the trampled thorn-fence of a corral-keeper" (54:31 / 45:13 as cited in the source).

The Qur'an does not give the details of this cry and blast, although elsewhere, in Surah Fussilat, the details are given, that...

﴿فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً مِّثْلَ صَاعِقَةِ عَادٍ وَثَمُودَ﴾ (41:13) "Say: I warn you of a sudden thunderbolt like the thunderbolt that befell 'Ad and Thamud."

It is also possible that ṣā'iqah is an attribute of ṣayḥah, meaning a crashing sound. It is also possible that ṣayḥah and ṣā'iqah are used for one reality, namely a sudden overtaking punishment. And it is also possible that ṣayḥah is the voice of the thunderbolt, or that the thunderbolt is the effect of the voice. How the voice was given, we do not know.

In any case, a crashing and thundering voice came upon them and annihilated them. They became like *hashīm al-muḥtazir* (like the trampled dry thorn-fence of the enclosure-builder). *Al-Muḥtazir* is the one who builds a *khaṭīrah* or enclosure, and he builds this enclosure from dry, thorny wood. These people became like dry, decayed wood that has broken and crumbled into chaff. The comparison is this: the enclosure-keeper gathers wood and tree branches for his livestock; the animals eat the branches, they dry out, and the animals trample them, so they are crushed like chaff. Thus this people became like the eaten and trampled bushes of the enclosure-keeper, by a single divine cry.

This is a severely painful and frightening scene, and it is a response to those who were corrupters and considered themselves great; thus those arrogant ones were ground down.

After this painful and frightening scene, people are directed to take admonition from the signs of Allah, to reflect, and to the Qur'an as the best guide for this purpose.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verse 32:

"And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?" (54:32; the passage cites 45:23 as a parallel reference). The curtain falls, and on the stage lies the trampled chaff. A scene for the eyes and a lesson for the heart. This Qur'an calls out loudly, calling those who take heed and those who reflect and ponder.

Now, when the curtain rises again, the page of history that lies close to the Arabian Peninsula is turned: the scene of the people of Lut (Lot):

The story of the people of Lut is related in detail in other places. Here the purpose is not to give the details of that story, but to admonish: to show what the outcome of denial is, namely that the severe punishment of Allah comes. For this reason the passage begins with the mention of denial of Allah's warnings.

﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ (54:33) "The people of Lut denied the warnings," and immediately after this the punishment of Allah is mentioned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verses 34–35:

"Indeed, We sent upon them a windstorm carrying pebbles. None remained except the family of Lut; We saved them before dawn by a favour from Us. Thus do We reward those who give thanks." (Qur'an 54:34–35)

Al-hasib is the wind that sweeps up pebbles and hurls them away. Elsewhere it is mentioned that stones of baked clay were rained down upon them. The very sound of the word "al-hasib" resembles the sound of stones being thrown. It carries an intensity and harshness that suits the scene and atmosphere at that moment. The account of Pharaoh, from beginning to end, is given in such brevity. Warners came to Pharaoh and his chiefs. They presented signs. They denied all those signs, and Allah seized them in the manner in which a party holding true power seizes. Mentioning honour and authority is meant to show that they were seized with great severity. The allusion is that Pharaoh spoke of great honour, strength and supreme authority, whereas all these matters belong to Allah. Before Allah, his false honour did not remain, his false supreme authority collapsed, and the true Sovereign seized him firmly and with great severity and lesson-giving force, just as they had been oppressing the weak in Egypt with harshness, tyranny and domineering force. In the same way, Allah destroyed them as well. Now the curtain falls on this final scene. This is the scene of Pharaoh the tyrant and a glimpse of it.

This was the last of the scenes of the punishment of deniers in human history. The memory of all the deniers is fresh in the minds of readers, and the feeling of listeners and viewers is still imprinted with those impressions, when the address to the people of Makkah begins. They are warned that you too can be utterly destroyed in the same way if you do not desist, and that the nature of your deeds actually demands that a punishment more terrible than this should come upon you:

"Akfarukum ................ mustatar (45: 34–55)"

"Are your disbelievers better than those? Or do you have an exemption written for you in the scriptures? Or do these people say that we are a strong group who will defend ourselves? Soon this group will be defeated and all of them will be seen turning their backs and fleeing. Rather, the real time of the promise to deal with them is the Resurrection, and it is a great calamity and a more bitter hour. These guilty people are indeed in error, and their intellect has been struck. On the day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, it will be said to them: now taste the touch of Hell."

We have created everything with a measure, and Our command is but one command, and it comes into effect in the blink of an eye. We have already destroyed many like you; is there then anyone who will accept advice? Whatever they have done is recorded in the registers, and every small and great matter is written down and present.

This is a warning of the punishments of both this world and the Hereafter, and it is declared that there is no doubt in it. It is declared that there is no path or opening to escape from it, and no hope of fleeing or being saved. Nor can any nimbleness be shown in reckoning and accounting, and in this way one cannot escape punishment.

You have seen what befell the deniers of the earlier nations. After all, what guarantee do you have that you will not meet the same end?

"Akfarukum ............ ula'ikum (45: 34)" — "Are your disbelievers better than those?" Of the disbelievers of earlier nations who were utterly destroyed in the same way, in what respect are you better than them?

"Am lakum ............ al-dabr (45: 34)" — "Or do you have an exemption written for you in the scriptures?" And by which these revealed scrolls bear witness that you would be free from the consequence of disbelief and denial. It is neither the case nor that. You are neither better than them, nor is your acquittal written in those scrolls. The only situation is that you too will meet the same end that they met, as Allah has decreed.

Now this address takes the form of a general address, and in it a strong expression of astonishment is made at their affair.

Or do they say, "We are a formidable host who will defend themselves"? When they saw that the Quraysh of Makkah were a large multitude, their resolve would swell, and, intoxicated by their own strength, they would say: "We shall remain victorious, no one can prevail over us, and no force can defeat us."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 54, verse 45:

"Soon this multitude will be defeated and they will be seen turning their backs and fleeing" (54:45). Therefore their multitude will not benefit them, and their strength will not prove a helper for them. This announcement came from Allah, the Subduer and the Compeller, so it happened in this way, and it had to happen in this way.

Muslim and Bukhari have related the narration of Ibn Abbas. He said that on the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in a platform that had been prepared for him, and he was supplicating: "O Allah, I beseech You by Your promise and Your covenant. If You wish, after today You will not be worshipped on this earth." Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) took him by the hand and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is sufficient for you; you have already implored your Lord greatly." He came out while wearing his armour, and he was saying:

"Soon this multitude will be defeated and they will be seen turning their backs and fleeing" (54:45).

In the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Ikrimah, he said: when this verse was revealed, "Soon this multitude will be defeated and they will be seen turning their backs and fleeing" (54:45), Umar (رضي الله عنه) said, "Which multitude will be defeated?" Umar says: when the day of Badr came, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wearing his armour and reciting this very verse: "Soon this multitude will be defeated and they will turn their backs and flee." Then at that moment I understood what multitude was meant by it.

This was the defeat of the world. But it was not the final defeat, nor is it the severe and bitter punishment. Therefore, after this worldly defeat, the discourse turns again to the final defeat.

Now it is explained in detail how the punishment of the Hour will be severe, intense and bitter, and the details are given within one of the scenes of the Day of Judgment:"

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verses 47–48:

Indeed the criminals are in error and in madness. On the Day they are dragged on their faces into the Fire, it will be said to them: "Taste the touch of Hell." (The Qur'an, 54:47–48) That is, they are in misguidance, where the mind and the spirit are punished, and they are in Hell, where the body and the skin are punished. This is because they used to say, and so did all people like them:

﴿Shall we follow a single human being from among ourselves? Then indeed we would be in error and madness.﴾ (54:24) Now they will come to know whether the error lies in following or in denying, and whether the Fire lies in following the Messenger or in opposing the Messenger.

They will be thrown face-first into the Fire with the utmost severity and contempt. This is because in the world they acted with arrogance and pride, and made decisions by relying on their power. Now here, along with physical punishment, they will also be given spiritual and psychological punishment, through reproach.

﴿Taste the touch of the Fire.﴾ (54:48)

Under the shadow of this terrifying and trembling scene, the address now turns toward all people, and toward the people of the Prophet ﷺ, so that the reality of Allah's wisdom, His planning, His decree and His judgments may settle in their hearts.

Whether it is this world or the Hereafter, the punishment of this world or the punishment of the Hereafter, the earlier messengers and warnings or the Qur'an and the Last Prophet, this entire universe or its management and order, whether a small thing or a great thing: all of them have been created according to a measure and a plan, in accordance with Allah's wisdom. Nothing has been created without purpose, by chance, in vain, or without thought.

﴿Indeed, We have created everything with measure.﴾ (Qur'an 54:49; the reference given in the text reads "45: 9 4")

Everything, whether small or large, whether it speaks or is silent, whether it moves or is still, whether it is a past thing, a present thing, a known thing or an unknown thing, Allah has created each thing according to a measure.

This measure (taqdir) determines its reality. It determines its attributes. It determines its quantity. It determines its time. It determines its place. It determines its relations with its environment. It determines its effects in this universe.

This Qur'anic verse consists of a few brief words, yet it points to a great and astonishing truth. The meaning of this verse encompasses this entire universe. The human heart grasps this truth only when it keeps this whole universe in mind, walks in step with it, derives facts from it, and perceives that this universe is a creation of mutual proportion and of very precise, interconnected order, in which everything has been made according to a measure. Only then will a shadow and an outline of this truth settle in the mind. Keeping only one thing in mind will not produce this understanding.

Modern science has encompassed some very minor fields of this truth. This knowledge has been gathered by modern science according to its limited means. Science has found that the distances between stars are according to a fixed measure. The planets, their sizes, the groups of stars and planets called galaxies, and their attraction to one another: these quantities and distances have become so precisely determined that scientists have fixed the distances of stars they have not even seen, because the requirement of attraction and harmony was that these stars should be at such a distance, since, according to the system they have observed and its design and decree, their distance ought to be that far. Afterwards, when they observed through powerful telescopes, it was found that the distances they had determined according to the measure, that is, according to calculation, were correct. In short, keeping these celestial bodies in this vast space at such fixed distances, with no change or alteration within them and no disturbance, is proof that Allah has made everything according to a fixed quantity, measure, or decree.

Knowledge of the sustenance and the measure found on this earth on which we live has grown so much that if even a slight change is made in its present state, shape, and proportions, the enormous variety of life upon it would suffer tremendous disruption, or life itself would end altogether. The volume of this earth, its mass, its distance from the sun, its temperature, the tilt of the earth on its axis, the speed of its rotation, the distance of the moon from the earth, the size and material of the moon, the division of the earth into water and land, and its proportion: in short, these and thousands of other such measures are those which the hand of power has ordained with exactness. If even a slight change occurred in them, the entire present system would change, and life would immediately vanish from the earth. The understanding of the balance among the laws that control life has reached such a level that the balance between living things and their environment, and the balance of all things with one another, has reached such a point, and humans have come to know it, that the indications pointing to the truth contained in this verse are well corroborated. Thus the relationship between the factors of life, the factors that sustain life, and the factors of death and extinction is also fixed in the living world. When any living creature exceeds its limits, the natural laws that control life themselves check it, so that every living creature's needs can be met.

Here it is necessary to point out that some living things have a connection and balance with other living things as well, and we have already pointed to the balance existing on the earth. (See Surah al-Furqan.)

Those birds which obtain food by hunting smaller birds are few in number. This is because they lay very few eggs, then bear few young, and they live in limited and specific areas, and their lifespan is long compared with other birds. If, along with their long lifespan, they also bore many young and could survive in every region, they would wipe out all the small birds from the world, and the species of small birds would be destroyed, or their number would become so small that the purpose for which Allah created them, namely the hunting and feeding of people and the countless other purposes they fulfil on the earth, would be lost. Someone has aptly said:

Bughath al-tayr (the scavenging bird) has many offspring,
but the mother of the falcon (shahin) bears few, and she is slow to produce young.

(The bughath, a water bird, has many young, but the mother of the shahin, the falcon, bears very few and only a small number of chicks.) This too is the wisdom and decree of Allah, as we have seen, so that the natural system does not fall into disorder, and so that a balance is created between the birth, survival, and destruction of birds by means of the flesh-eating birds.

A housefly lays several million eggs, but its lifespan is only about two weeks. If it lived for many years and laid eggs in the same proportion, flies would cover the surface of the earth within a short time, and many living animals, and even humans, would perish, or life on the surface of the earth would become difficult. But the system of natural balance is at work, and this balance is in the hand of Allah. If the offspring of a creature are many, its lifespan has been made short, and if its offspring are few, its lifespan has been made long. We wish to present this matter in the detailed discussion of life.

Those creatures that can be seen only through a microscope are greater in number than all other living things, and they spread in enormous abundance and are very harmful. Yet they are very weak in sustaining life and very short-lived. By the millions and billions they die from cold, they die from heat, they die from the rays of the sun, from germicidal medicines and other causes and means, and these things can harm a limited number of humans and animals. If these things were strong or lived longer, they would become a danger to living things and to humans.

Allah has given every living creature weapons for protection from its enemies, and these weapons differ for each creature according to its need. For example, some have been given the armour of numbers, some have been given the power of grip, and some have been given [other means of defence].

Small snakes have been given venom, or the weapon of very swift flight. Cobras have been given large muscular weapons, so venom is rare among them, and the cobra is unable to save itself by other means. Therefore a substance has been given to it that stains and gives off a foul odour, so that whoever touches it is splashed with that material. In this way it protects itself from its enemies.

The egg into which the sperm cell has entered attaches itself to the wall of the womb. It begins to feed upon the womb and creates around itself a hollow in the womb which fills with blood, and it remains alive in that and keeps sucking the blood. The cord that connects the womb with the navel of the child supplies blood until the time of delivery, and this cord has been created for this very purpose. This cord is neither too long nor too short, and its length has been decreed in such a measure that it fulfils its purpose well.

In the final days of pregnancy, a substance begins to form within the breasts, and after delivery a yellowish substance (milk) flows out. Behold the craftsmanship of Allah's workmanship: within it is the substance that protects the child from infectious diseases. Milk begins to flow on the second day after the child's birth, and observe the arrangement of nature: the milk increases gradually. After one year it reaches one and a half litres, although in the early days its quantity is small. The miracle is not only that as the child grows, the milk also increases, but the composition of the milk also changes. At first it is merely water and sugar, and after that the other essential substances increase in it, and then fat is also present in it. Indeed, each day's milk differs from the milk of the following day, in accordance with the child's needs for growth and development.

Countless mechanisms operate in the growth of a human being. The duties of a human being and the many factors engaged in his manner of functioning, which preserve his life and guard his health, and these factors which are installed within the human body as factories, have yielded strange and astonishing information. From these it is evident that the hand of power has arranged a system of such fine detail, and that its arrangements are being carried out, and from them it is clearly seen that the system of Allah is at work. These factors operate for every individual and every organ, indeed work is being done for every cell, and nothing is hidden from the sight of Allah. We cannot give here the details of the structure of the human body and its intricate system, but as an example we briefly point to just one system. This is the system of the endocrine glands. These are small factories within the body which supply the body with the chemical substances it needs. Their power is such that even one of their thousand billion components produces a substance that is very important for the human body, and their system has been constructed such that the secretion of one gland is an essential component of the secretion of another gland. What has been learned about them until today is that their system is extremely complex, and if any single gland is disturbed, a process of general destruction begins in the human body, even if that disturbance lasts only a short time.

As for animals, their defensive systems and weapons differ according to their species and kinds, and they have been given strength according to their needs.

Lions, tigers, beasts of prey, and other carnivorous animals have been given mouths capable of seizing their prey. All animals whose sustenance depends upon hunting other animals have been given claws, sharp teeth, and strong jaws for this purpose. And since in attacking they rely upon their nerves and muscles, the muscles of their legs are very hard. The claws of their hands and feet are very hard and strong, and within their stomachs there are acidic secretions of this kind which digest flesh and bones in a short time.

Likewise, the digestive systems of grazing animals and domestic animals have been fashioned according to their diet. For example, the digestive system of animals that subsist by grazing is entirely different. Their mouths are relatively wide, and these animals do not possess strong claws. Likewise, they have no strong fangs for tearing. In contrast, their teeth are such that they cut and grind grass. They eat grass and vegetation very swiftly and soon swallow it. Thus they perform for humans the services for which they were created. The hand of power has given a wondrous digestive system: what grazing animals eat collects in a pouch. When the animal's daily work is over and it rests, all its food passes into an empty chamber called the "cap" (reticulum). From there it returns to the mouth. Now it is chewed and ground again thoroughly, and it passes into the third chamber called the omasum. After that it goes to the fourth chamber, called the abomasum. This lengthy digestive system has been created only for the animal, because grazing and ruminant animals are hunted, and therefore they need to store their food quickly and then go and digest it at leisure. Modern sciences have discovered that the process of rumination is essential for the life of these animals, because grass that is not quickly digested, since all the cells of plants are covered with a cellulose membrane, requires a very long time to be digested. If there were no system of rumination and no special storage in their stomach, they would have to spend a long time in the pasture. It is possible that the whole day would be spent in digesting grass, and even then they could not complete their nourishment, and the whole day would be spent in eating and chewing food. They eat grass quickly and store it, and then ruminate when it has become quite soft within the storage. In this way several purposes of animals are fulfilled. They can also do good work, and their food is also thoroughly digested. These are the arrangements of the Lord, may He be exalted.

Birds that eat flesh, such as the owl and the hawk, have beaks shaped like a bow, which are sharp and capable of tearing flesh. Aquatic animals such as the duck and the mallard have been given broad beaks, so that they may seek their food in water and mud, and their beaks have small projections like teeth, which help in cutting insects and the like.

As for hens, pigeons, and other birds that pick up grain from the ground and eat it, they have been given small beaks and slender heads. They pick up even the smallest grain. The heron, on the other hand, has a long beak, and beneath it there is a pouch shaped like a sock. It serves as a fisherman's net, because its food is fish.

The hoopoe and the [ruffled bird] have beaks that are sharp and long, suitable for finding and eating insects and worms, because these things are beneath the ground. Science has discovered that by merely glancing at the beak of a bird, one can determine what its food is.

This commentary has now grown lengthy, and we are departing from the method Fi Zilal al-Quran has adopted. If we were to discuss every kind of animal and livestock, the discussion would become far too long. Let us take just one example, the amoeba, which has a single cell. Observe how the Power of Divine Creation has met its needs and made complete provision for its requirements. The amoeba is an extremely minute-bodied creature. It is found in ponds, ditches, and on stones lying at the bottom of water. It has no eyes to see with. It is a shapeless, loose-bodied living thing, and it changes its form according to circumstances and needs. When it moves, it pushes forward some parts of its body to reach the desired place. These extra parts are called pseudopodia, or "small feet." If it finds food, it seizes it with one or two of these small feet. It then releases a digestive fluid onto the food, eats what it needs, and throws away the rest. It takes in oxygen from the water and breathes through its whole body. Consider a creature that does not see at all, yet it lives, moves, obtains food, breathes, expels its waste, and when it matures it splits into two parts, and these become two different creatures, exactly as a modern... 

Life in plants is likewise astonishing. In its wonders, it is in no way less than the wonders of humans, animals, and birds, and the workmanship of the Power of Divine Creation is in no way less within plants than within those animals. This is the meaning of this verse:

﴿And He created everything and measured it with precise measure.﴾

That is, Allah has created everything according to a predetermined measure. This is a very great principle, and it is all-encompassing. For example, every movement of this universe and every event, whether small or great, proceeds in accordance with Allah's decree (qadar) and His management (tadbir). Every movement in human history, every movement of the human soul, breathing in and breathing out, is predetermined. The time, place, and environment of every soul are fixed and predetermined, and its life is linked with the movement of this universe, and it lies within the same reckoning as the great events within the scope of that reckoning.

Far off in a desert, a lone tree stands. Destiny has caused it to stand, and there must be a need for it. This tree too is performing some duty assigned to it, and it too is linked with the system of this entire universe. This ant walking on the ground, this particle floating in the air, and this cell swimming in the water are likewise predetermined, just like the heavenly bodies, and they move by someone's command.

The decree of Allah operates in time, it operates in space, its quantity is predetermined, its form is predetermined, and all conditions and all principles are predetermined.

How the system of qada wa qadar (divine decree and predestination) of Allah operates can be seen in an example: Hadrat Ya'qub (peace be upon him) married another woman, and from her Yusuf and Binyamin were born. Some have thought that this was apparently a personal decision, but behind it the Power of Divine Creation was at work so that the brothers of Yusuf would envy them, throw him into a dark well, from there a caravan would pick him up, sell him in Egypt, in Egypt there is the house of the Aziz of Egypt, his wife would try to seduce him, he would prove himself exalted and superior, and he would be sent to prison. Why? So that in prison he would meet the servants of the king and explain to them the interpretation of dreams. Why? Until now no purpose of these events is apparent. The question may arise: why did all this happen? Hadrat Yusuf, though innocent, is suffering torment in prison; then what was Ya'qub's (peace be upon him) fault? Why was he burning? Why did he lose his sight through grief and sorrow? And why were these afflictions inflicted upon Yusuf (peace be upon him)? Bodily and spiritual afflictions. After a full twenty-five years had passed, the first answer came: destiny was preparing him to rule Egypt so that Egypt and its neighboring lands could be saved from famine. Then why? So that he might bring his parents and brothers to Egypt. Then so that from their lineage the nation of Bani Isra'il would grow up, so that Fir'awn would inflict oppression upon them, and so that Musa (peace be upon him) would be sent for them. All this happened so that on this earth those events would take place which occurred after Yusuf was thrown into the well. The effects of those events are present in this world even today, and they continue to influence the events of the world.

Then there is another event. The grandfather of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), Abu al-Anbiya' Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him), went to Egypt and married the Egyptian woman Hajarah. This too was not a personal matter. This, and the events that occurred earlier in the life of Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him), as a result of which he left his homeland, from Iraq to Kan'an and from there to Egypt, and from there the bringing of Hajarah, the birth of Isma'il (peace be upon him), settling him in the House of Allah (Bayt Allah), so that Muhammad (ﷺ) would be born from the lineage of Ibrahim, in this Arabian peninsula, which is the best place on this earth and the center of the Islamic call, so that as a result a great event would take place in the history of humanity.

This too is the decree of Allah, and its far end is in the hand of the Power of Divine Creation. Every event and every occurrence emerges from there. The beginning is from there, the end is there too, and in every step and every change there is the hand of the Power of Divine Creation... This is the system of Allah's decree; it is in force, it is comprehensive and all-inclusive, subtle and profound.

Man sees only the nearest end of this, but he does not see the other end of the long rope of causes, and sometimes this rope becomes very long. Ages pass, we travel very far, and we do not see the chain of destiny and management. We do not understand how:

*Do not let the fly enter the garden,*
*For the moth's blood would be shed unjustly.*

How will it be? People hurry over this, they make an uproar, and they bring forth new proposals. In reality, these people are placing themselves in torment. They lay hands on the system of qada wa qadar.

Allah plainly states that He has created everything with a fixed measure. People should leave the outcomes to the One who owns the outcomes, and work at ease. They should move in harmony with Allah's system, qada and qadar. With the utmost affection and kindness they should do their share of the work, and with the utmost steadfastness and reliance upon Allah, they should keep advancing.

As for the revolution of Allah, it can emerge in the blink of an eye. Allah can do everything.

﴿Our command is but a single word, like the blink of an eye.﴾ (45: 0 5) A single signal and a single word complete every task: the small matter and the great upheaval alike. For God there is nothing great or small. These distinctions belong to human affairs, in which some matters are large and some small. With God there is no time, no place, and no blinking of an eye. There it is only Kun fayakun (Be, and it is). The examples of great, small, and very brief durations are given to help human beings understand. What is time? It is a small human notion, measured by the earth's rotation on its axis and its annual revolution. God's reckoning of time is not this. That notion is very limited.

One word brings this whole universe into existence. One word brings change into it. One word will bring it to an end. One word gives existence to everything. One word spreads life. One word gives death, and one word will raise the dead again. By one word the Resurrection will take place, along with the gathering and the scattering, and the reckoning and the account. A single word, a single will: no struggle is needed, and no time or place is required. There is only power, there is only decree, and everything is easy for God.

And it was by this same word that We destroyed past peoples and wiped them away. Just look at history.

﴿And We have certainly destroyed many like you. Is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ ﴿Everything they have done is recorded in the scriptures, and every small and great matter is inscribed.﴾ These are the ruins of the deniers (mukadhdhibin), to which the surah itself alludes. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 54, verses 54–55:

ان المتقین ............ مقتدر (55) (45:45 ۔ 55) "Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and rivers, in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful." (45:45–55)

The criminals were in error and in the Fire. The God-fearing are among springs and rivers. The criminals will be dragged on their faces into Hell, with contempt, and then, as a rebuke, it will be said:

ذوقو ............ سفر "Taste the touch of the Fire." While the believers are in gardens and rivers, in places of honour, in the presence of the All-Powerful Sovereign. There is a complete contrast between the two.

The use of words here is also remarkable. The word jannat (gardens) together with nahr (rivers) carries a very complete meaning: gardens and rivers from which blessings and ease become apparent. The word nahr, being of the same metrical weight as the word Saqar, also has a very gentle pronunciation; that is, the soft, easily uttered word signals that they have every kind of facility available. It is a miracle of the Quran that meaning is conveyed not only by sense but also by pronunciation, just as Saqar conveys harshness.

Besides the blessings of body and tongue, there will also be provision for the nourishment of heart and soul, and that is nearness to the Sovereign of all power.

Fi ............ muqtadir (45:55) "In a seat of truth, in the presence of the All-Powerful Sovereign." This is a place of permanent tranquillity, a nearness of the utmost honour. They will feel love within that nearness, and they will be content. This is because in the world these people were fearers of Allah, always awaiting the pleasure of Allah, and Allah's system is that He does not gather two fears in one heart, so that one who fears Allah in the world should also fear Him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fears here will be content and joyful there, and along with feeling peace and tranquillity in that terrifying and dreadful field, the people of faith will also attain honour and dignity.

Here this melody comes to its very gentle close. The God-fearing are here in a secure shade, and this Surah, all of whose links were in the form of a terrifying explosion, seizing and dragging, ends with this final scene of the peaceful conditions of the believers, in which their bodies, hearts and souls all appear peaceful and content. This is the manner of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. What is said penetrates to the depths of hearts, because Allah is Subtle and Aware, and it is He who created everything according to a measure, and He knows well how to deal with everything.

The use of words here is also remarkable. The word jannat (gardens) together with nahr (rivers) carries a very complete meaning: gardens and rivers from which blessings and ease become apparent. The word nahr, being of the same metrical weight as the word Saqar, also has a very gentle pronunciation; that is, the soft, easily uttered word signals that they have every kind of facility available. It is a miracle of the Quran that meaning is conveyed not only by sense but also by pronunciation, just as Saqar conveys harshness.

Besides the blessings of body and tongue, there will also be provision for the nourishment of heart and soul, and that is nearness to the Sovereign of all power.

Fi ............ muqtadir (45:55) "In a seat of truth, in the presence of the All-Powerful Sovereign." This is a place of permanent tranquillity, a nearness of the utmost honour. They will feel love within that nearness, and they will be content. This is because in the world these people were fearers of Allah, always awaiting the pleasure of Allah, and Allah's system is that He does not gather two fears in one heart, so that one who fears Allah in the world should also fear Him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fears here will be content and joyful there, and along with feeling peace and tranquillity in that terrifying and dreadful field, the people of faith will also attain honour and dignity.

Here this melody comes to its very gentle close. The God-fearing are here in a secure shade, and this Surah, all of whose links were in the form of a terrifying explosion, seizing and dragging, ends with this final scene of the peaceful conditions of the believers, in which their bodies, hearts and souls all appear peaceful and content. This is the manner of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. What is said penetrates to the depths of hearts, because Allah is Subtle and Aware, and it is He who created everything according to a measure, and He knows well how to deal with everything.
